newsitem.title: USA: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Mkt hinges on data, Greenspan.
newsitem.headline: US CREDIT OUTLOOK -- Mkt hinges on data, Greenspan.

text.p: Tuesday has the potential to be a make-it-or-break-it day in the U.S. Treasury market, as two crucial economic numbers will be released, while Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan speaks early in the session, players said.

With the market badly beaten up from Friday's stronger-than-expected December employment report, players said the only thing that can rescue the market is weak economic news and comforting news from Greenspan.
"We need some pleasant surprises to help this market," said Joseph Liro, chief economist at CIBC Wood Gundy Securities Corp. "The environment is a lot more negative than a week ago."

Players noted that while a strong dollar and falling oil prices would have been plusses for the market in recent weeks and months, those factors failed to bring Treasuries out of their doldrums on Monday. So, the market looks to Tuesday for some direction. At 0830 EST/1330 GMT, the Labor Department releases the December consumer price report, while the Commerce Department's December retail sales data are due.

Overall CPI is expected to have risen 0.3 percent, while CPI excluding food and energy prices are seen up 0.2 percent in December, according to a Reuters poll. Meanwhile, retail sales is expected to have increased 0.5 percent, with retail sales ex-automobiles seen up 0.4 percent in December.

Analysts said that while numbers at consensus would have helped the market as late as last week, bond players now require numbers significantly lower than consensus to boost bond prices. And, they added, in the case of retail sales, a substantial upaward revision to November's 0.4 percent drop would be a negative.

"If we get a strong December print and an upward revision to November, the market will not forgive it," Liro said. "The market has been complacent for so long, buying hook, line and sinker that we have moderate growth and sooft inflation. So, when three weeks ago when we started to get stronger economic numbers, culminating with the strong employment report Friday, that complacency has been rattled.
"We have shifted sentiment from a neutral to accommodative Fed to concerns of tightening," he said, adding that the odds of a Fed tightening in the first quarter are still slim.
Ahead of the data, overseas markets will keep an eye on Greenspan, with implications seen spilling into the U.S. session should the Fed chief say something the market does or doesn't like.

At 0430 EST/1630 GMT, Greenspan is slated to discuss central banking and global finance at a seminar sponsored by Leuven KUL University in Belgium. Greenspan will also receive an honarary degree from the University.
In late Monday trading, the 30-year bond was at 95-17/32, down 2/32, to yield 6.85 percent.
